class_guard:
SPEC (one module owns every shared value; every consumer asks it; nothing else may compute one).
1. feeds.py owns every store-, payer- or period-wide value derived from data. Each function takes (conn, today), clamps to today, and returns the value with its basis (inputs used, their volume share, inputs set aside and why), cached per run and stored in meta feeds:values:
   a. coverage(): per payer group, intervals over which its remittances are believed complete: payment days (each clamped to the day its file arrived) no more than max(14, 2 x the group's median gap) apart; an interval counts once it holds 3 payment days or spans 14 days (a lone file after a gap opens an interval that does not count yet). payer_through(g) = end of g's last counted interval. judgeable(g, sent, due) = one counted interval covers both. feed_date() = volume-weighted median of payer_through over groups holding >= 1% of the last 120 days' remittance lines (>= 3 groups; else the clamped newest, as H8). Reference: guard/L1/reference_feed.py.
   b. production_through(): end of the continuous posted coverage of the current Production boxes; production_fresh = today - production_through <= 14; covered(svc, answer window) per box.
   c. group_posting(g): an EMA payer group counts as posting only with >= 3 checks (or >= 5% of its usual checks) inside that coverage.
   d. ar_as_of(file): 99th percentile of aging dates, capped at the day the file arrived; rank A/R snapshots by it.
   e. export_rank(rows/file): by content dates (99th percentile of submission, denial, transaction, posted dates), then received_at; never a workbook stamp or a file name; a row older by content never overrides a newer status.
   f. provider_tier(npi): reference from the Medicare fee schedule tables (pfs/mpfs), or the median of NPIs with >= 20 lines; under the floor -> 'unknown'.
   g. any 'most common' or majority value (EMA payer -> group votes, write-off sign, claim prefix): minimum count (>= 5 claims or >= 20 rows) and >= 80% share, else 'unknown' with the documented safe default (longest common filing limit, hold).
   h. every window (alerts, pattern watch, answer times, turnaround, recovery maturity, fee 'now', ratios, owner figures, C1 check causes) is anchored on feed_date or payer_through, never on a raw MAX/MIN.
2. The clock is not a data date. Due dates, follow-ups, 'To decide', deadline counts and scoreboard windows count from today (the practice's date). Data dates answer only 'can the answer be seen' (judgeable); when it cannot, the item stays listed as 'cannot check' with its dollars and the reason, never frozen, dropped or flooded.
3. Door clamps (with L2): an 835 whose payment date is after the day it was read (+1 day) or before 2000, a line whose service date is after its payment date, and an EMA row dated after its file's arrival are held with a plain reason on the Data tab and never reach the store until a person releases them (the live image has 0 such rows, so nothing real is held). The EMA report readers' date_bounds already do this for Production and A/R.
4. Movement record and hold (with L3's swing guard): each run compares feeds:values with the last run's. A move beyond a threshold (feed date or any payer_through by > 7 days, Production or A/R freshness flipping, any provider tier, export rank changing the status of > 20 claims, any alert set clearing by > 3) writes one decision-log row with the old and new value and their basis; the automatic effects it causes (items appearing or closing for payers with no new data, holds lifting, alerts clearing) are held for one person on the Data tab ('Remittances: 38 payers current through Oct 9; Humana alone through Nov 20, one file'), and the old value stays in force until released. Each item's 'Why did this change?' cites the shared value and basis that moved it.
5. Lint (CI, all four environments): test_every_module_takes_store_wide_data_dates_from_one_owner fails when any module except feeds.py runs MAX/MIN over payment_date, posted, last_posted, as_of or ingested_at without GROUP BY or a per-row key, or Python max()/min() over those fields of all lines, unless the site is in an allowlist with a one-line reason (display only, per-claim). Today it lists 60 sites (30 for the newest payment date).
Ports: hotfix 2's H8 tests move into push 2 unchanged (backlog INT), then the stronger coverage rule replaces its 'latest date per group' (H8 still bridges a gap with one day of files).
property_test:
Non-interference of one input (a generated, metamorphic test, run on both store kinds: the server's file store and the compact in-memory image cloud.py builds).
Generate a world from a seed: k in [3, 8] payer groups paying weekly or biweekly with random volumes (a few irregular gaps), 20-60 weeks of 835s ending on a random day, the weekly EMA exports for the same claims, optionally Production boxes and an A/R, 2-10 NPIs (Medicare E/M lines). Run the daily cycle with today fixed; record S0 = {item id: signal, state, hold, deadline, severity, work_now membership, expected-value rank} and V0 = feeds.values() with bases.
Add exactly ONE perturbation x drawn from: an 835 from one group (adjustment-only, or <= 3 claims) paid today-3, today+1, today+400, 2099-12-31 or 2000-01-01; a one-day multi-payer bundle after a hole of >= 3 weeks; one service line dated a year ahead; a weekly export re-saved with a newer workbook stamp and older content (and a CSV with a different file name); a Production file covering <= 3 posted days; an A/R with one row dated ahead; one Medicare line from a new NPI at +/-10-30%; one EMA check row for one group; one 835 for a group from years before the archive. Run the cycle again: S1, V1.
Assert: (1) every date in V1 is <= today, and x is held at the door when its own dates are after the day it was read; (2) every shared value whose basis does not include a quorum of inputs touched by x (>= 50% of the relevant volume, or the stated minimum count) is unchanged; (3) for every item whose claim and payer group x does not touch, signal, state, hold, deadline, severity and work_now membership are identical in S0 and S1; (4) every difference allowed by (2) or (3) carries a decision-log row naming the shared value, its old and new value and basis, and is held for a person, never applied silently; (5) the blindness banner, STALE_FEED and the fax hold are not switched off by x alone. Shrink a failure to the minimal x and world. Seed the run with today's 16 hand-written cases in guard/L1/test_l1_shared_values.py (15 fail on the snapshot; the reference guard passes).
